final_answer:
Let
\[
I_n=\iint_{\mathbb R^2}e^{-n(x^4+x^2y^2+y^6)}\,dx\,dy.
\]
The integrand is even in both variables. Put
\[
a=x^2,\qquad b=y^2.
\]
Since \(dx\,dy=(4\sqrt{ab})^{-1}\,da\,db\) on the first quadrant and there are four quadrants,
\[
I_n=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
a^{-1/2}b^{-1/2}e^{-n(a^2+ab+b^3)}\,da\,db.
\]
Now scale \(a=n^{-1/2}s\) and \(z=n^{1/2}b\). Then
\[
I_n=n^{-1/2}\int_0^\infty z^{-1/2}e^{-z^3/n^{1/2}}F(z)\,dz,
\]
where
\[
F(z)=\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}e^{-s^2-zs}\,ds.
\]
Thus
\[
\sqrt n\,I_n=A_N:=\int_0^\infty e^{-z^3/N}g(z)\,dz,
\qquad N=n^{1/2},
\]
with
\[
g(z)=z^{-1/2}F(z).
\]

For large \(z\), substitute \(t=zs\):
\[
F(z)=z^{-1/2}\int_0^\infty t^{-1/2}e^{-t}e^{-t^2/z^2}\,dt
=z^{-1/2}\left(\sqrt\pi+O(z^{-2})\right).
\]
Hence
\[
g(z)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{z}+O(z^{-3}).
\]
So the logarithmic divergence has coefficient \(\sqrt\pi\), cut off at scale \(z^3\sim N\), giving coefficient
\[
\sqrt\pi\cdot \frac13\log N=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{6}\log n.
\]

It remains to compute the constant term. Define
\[
K=\int_0^1 g(z)\,dz+\int_1^\infty\left(g(z)-\frac{\sqrt\pi}{z}\right)\,dz.
\]
We compute \(K\) from the Mellin transform. For \(1/2<p<1\),
\[
\int_0^\infty z^{p-1}g(z)\,dz
=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
z^{p-3/2}s^{-1/2}e^{-s^2-zs}\,ds\,dz.
\]
Integrating first in \(z\),
\[
\int_0^\infty z^{p-3/2}e^{-zs}\,dz
=\Gamma\!\left(p-\frac12\right)s^{-p+1/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\int_0^\infty z^{p-1}g(z)\,dz
=\Gamma\!\left(p-\frac12\right)\int_0^\infty s^{-p}e^{-s^2}\,ds
=\frac12\Gamma\!\left(p-\frac12\right)\Gamma\!\left(\frac{1-p}{2}\right).
\]
As \(p\to1^-\),
\[
\Gamma\!\left(\frac{1-p}{2}\right)=\frac{2}{1-p}-\gamma+O(1-p),
\]
and
\[
\Gamma\!\left(p-\frac12\right)
=\sqrt\pi\left(1-(1-p)\psi(1/2)+O((1-p)^2)\right),
\]
with \(\psi(1/2)=-\gamma-2\log2\). Hence
\[
\frac12\Gamma\!\left(p-\frac12\right)\Gamma\!\left(\frac{1-p}{2}\right)
=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{1-p}
+\sqrt\pi\left(\frac{\gamma}{2}+2\log2\right)+o(1).
\]
Since the pole \(\sqrt\pi/(1-p)\) corresponds exactly to the tail \(\sqrt\pi/z\), we get
\[
K=\sqrt\pi\left(\frac{\gamma}{2}+2\log2\right).
\]

Now split
\[
A_N=\int_0^\infty e^{-z^3/N}
\left(g(z)-\frac{\sqrt\pi}{z}\mathbf 1_{z\ge1}\right)\,dz
+\sqrt\pi\int_1^\infty \frac{e^{-z^3/N}}{z}\,dz.
\]
The first integral tends to \(K\). For the second, put \(u=z^3/N\):
\[
\int_1^\infty \frac{e^{-z^3/N}}{z}\,dz
=\frac13\int_{1/N}^\infty \frac{e^{-u}}u\,du
=\frac13\log N-\frac{\gamma}{3}+o(1).
\]
Therefore
\[
A_N-\frac{\sqrt\pi}{3}\log N
\to
K-\frac{\sqrt\pi\gamma}{3}.
\]
Since \(N=n^{1/2}\), \(\frac{\sqrt\pi}{3}\log N=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{6}\log n\). Thus
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\left(\sqrt n\,I_n-\frac{\sqrt\pi}{6}\log n\right)
=
\sqrt\pi\left(\frac{\gamma}{2}+2\log2-\frac{\gamma}{3}\right).
\]

\[
\boxed{\sqrt\pi\left(2\log2+\frac{\gamma}{6}\right)}
\]
